warnings.reason: GCC inlines the allocation injection harness malloc/free replacements for global operator new/delete and emits -Wmismatched-new-delete at allocation.cpp:20. These are test harness replacement functions; model/sanitizer builds have no warnings.

proofs: Forward pairs: (i+2)(i+3)-i(i+1)=4i+6; next difference is 4i+14. target*4+6<mod ensures a single modular add/subtract suffices.
Backward pairs: i(i-1)-(i-2)(i-3)=4i-6; next difference is 4i-14. Products use uint64_t; target<mod<=INT_MAX prevents overflow.
Wilson: ifac[k]=(-1)^(k+1)*fac[p-1-k]. Only newly added ifac indices are overwritten.
compatibility: std::vector storage/copy/move and resize rollback unchanged
small extension (<4096 added elements) uses original factorial and inverse factorial loops
only baseline Mint APIs are required; Wilson unary minus is constrained and otherwise original inverse recurrence is used

rejected_candidates.initial_measurement_scope: Initial official-case results correspond to rejected sources and are not presented as final performance.

limits: Measurements cover listed inputs, not a proof that every operation is universally faster. Online timing after this Mint change is unverified.
Forced no-int128 tests select the library standard arithmetic fallback; ACL itself may still use unsigned __int128 internally.
Allocation injection uses replacement new/delete in test code only and emits GCC harness warnings; library warnings0.
Counts of validation checks include table elements and repeated configurations, not distinct random cases.

Some cached/Lucas queries remain slower in isolated microbenchmarks; this change does not satisfy a universal no-slowdown claim. Table construction and representative full-program cases improve, but input distribution changes the benefit.
